newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New talks could finalise Russian-EU steel deal.
newsitem.headline: New talks could finalise Russian-EU steel deal.

text.p: Russian and European Community negotiators could finalise a long-awaited agreement on Russian steel exports at talks which begin on Thursday in Moscow, an EC official told Reuters.
Russia hopes a deal will open up the European market to Russian steel exports over the next five years.
"The team arrives and talks will start today. We hope this will be the last set of talks, and of course everybody hopes to finish the negotiations today," said the EC official.
Russian trade officials also hoped that the deal, which will replace an existing agreement which expires in June, would be clinched this week.
"This agreement will be fundamentally different from the current one. Its goal is to create a situation where EC limits on Russian steel imports can be removed," a Russian official said.

He said the new agreement would last five years and would eliminate current EC steel import quotas if Russia brings its steel industry into line with EC environmental norms and regulations on competition and state subsidies.
Russia has boosted exports to Europe in recent years due to falling domestic demand.

But the EC, worried about Russia "dumping" cheap steel exports, has insisted on quotas of 350,000 tonnes and 450,000 tonnes on Russian steel exports to the European Union and the former East Germany, respectively .

"The European position is, yes, we are ready to liberalise our market, but the Russian steel industry is in need of restructuring, so that it can be competitive and avoid being accused of dumping," the EC source said.
Russian 1996 steel output fell five percent from 1995 levels to 49.2 million tonnes, half peak levels from the late 1980s.
Russia consumes around 17 million tonnes annually, according to the International Iron and Steel Institute.
